pack.title: HIPAA, as it bears on AI
pack.publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (this pack is GovWren's own summary)
pack.attribution: Provisions of the HIPAA Security, Privacy, and Breach Notification Rules that bear on AI, each summarized in a sentence. It is not the regulatory text and not legal advice. It covers the rules as written, not what has been proposed. Read the regulation, and ask your privacy officer, for what applies to you.

requirements.title: HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR 164 Subpart C)

children.title: Risk analysis
children.text: Assess risks to electronic PHI across every system that holds or moves it, including AI tools, agents, and AI vendors.

children.title: Risk management
children.text: Put measures in place that bring identified risks down to a reasonable level.

children.title: Information system activity review
children.text: Regularly review records of system activity, such as audit logs and access reports.

children.title: Assigned security responsibility
children.text: Name the official responsible for security policies and procedures.

children.title: Information access management
children.text: Authorize access to electronic PHI, including access by service accounts and agents.

children.title: Security awareness and training
children.text: Train the workforce on security, including safe use of AI tools.

children.title: Security incident procedures
children.text: Identify, respond to, and document security incidents.

children.title: Contingency plan
children.text: Plan for emergencies that damage systems holding electronic PHI.

children.title: Evaluation
children.text: Periodically evaluate whether safeguards still meet the rule, including after changes.

children.title: Business associate contracts
children.text: Obtain satisfactory assurances from business associates that handle electronic PHI.

children.title: Access control
children.text: Technical controls limit access to electronic PHI to authorized people and software.

children.title: Audit controls
children.text: Record and examine activity in systems that contain or use electronic PHI.

children.title: Integrity
children.text: Protect electronic PHI from improper change or destruction.

children.title: Person or entity authentication
children.text: Verify that a person or entity seeking access is who they claim to be.

children.title: Transmission security
children.text: Guard electronic PHI sent over networks.

children.title: Documentation and retention
children.text: Keep required policies, procedures, and assessments in writing for six years and review them.

requirements.title: HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR 164 Subpart E)

children.title: Minimum necessary
children.text: Use or disclose only the PHI needed for the purpose.

children.title: Disclosures to business associates
children.text: Disclose PHI to a business associate only under a business associate agreement.

children.title: Authorization
children.text: Get a valid authorization where no other permission applies, including some research uses.

children.title: Research waivers
children.text: Use PHI for research without authorization only with an IRB or privacy board waiver or another listed pathway.

children.title: De-identification
children.text: De-identify by Safe Harbor or Expert Determination before treating data as outside the rule.

children.title: Limited data sets
children.text: Share a limited data set only under a data use agreement.

children.title: Administrative safeguards for PHI
children.text: Protect PHI from intentional or accidental misuse, including through AI prompts and outputs.

requirements.title: Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR 164 Subpart D)

children.title: Breach risk assessment
children.text: Presume an impermissible disclosure is a breach unless a documented risk assessment shows a low probability of compromise.

children.title: Notification
children.text: Notify individuals, HHS, and in some cases the media within the required times.
